questions.q: According to Poe, what should a writer settle before writing a word?
choices: The premise the work will prove
The ending, so every incident can lead toward it
The hero's ordinary world
The three dimensions of each character
questions.explain: Poe says every plot worth the name must be worked out to its dénouement before anything is attempted with the pen.

questions.q: A writer has a striking plot but no idea what feeling the piece should leave. What would Poe tell them to decide first?
choices: The single effect, the one impression the work should produce
Which value the climax should turn
Which archetypes their characters wear
The order of the 31 functions
questions.explain: Poe starts from the intended effect and chooses incidents and tone to produce it.

questions.q: Why does Poe insist a work be short enough to read at one sitting?
choices: Magazines paid by the line
Aristotle required it
Long works can't have reversals
Once the reader stops, the world intrudes and the single impression is broken
questions.explain: For Poe, unity of impression depends on reading without interruption.

questions.q: How does Poe's idea of unity differ from Aristotle's?
choices: Poe wants unity of time and place
Poe wants one hero, Aristotle one action
Aristotle wants one unified action; Poe wants one unified effect on the reader
They mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: Aristotle's unity is in the plot; Poe's is in the impression the work makes.

questions.q: A feature writer finds her last line before drafting, then shapes everything toward it. Whose method is this closest to?
choices: Forster's 'and then?'
Egri's bone structure
Propp's functions
Poe's working back from the end
questions.explain: Knowing the kicker first and writing toward it is Poe's ending-first method applied to journalism.

questions.q: Why did Poe say he chose 'Nevermore' as the refrain?
choices: It was the raven's real name
He wanted a single word with sonorous sounds whose meaning could shift each time
It was the poem's premise
It was borrowed from Hawthorne
questions.explain: He wanted a long o and an r, and one word that could be repeated with changing meaning.

questions.q: What is the main doubt critics raise about 'The Philosophy of Composition'?
choices: That it may be a performance or after-the-fact rationalization, not a true account
That Poe never wrote 'The Raven'
That it was translated badly
That it recommends long poems
questions.explain: Many readers, including T. S. Eliot, doubted the poem was really composed so coolly.

ideas: Decide the single effect you want to leave on the reader before you choose a single incident.
A work too long to be read at one sitting loses the unity of impression that gives it power.
A long poem is really a string of short poems joined by flat stretches.
Writers like to pretend they compose in a frenzy of inspiration, but a great poem can be built as deliberately as a solution to a mathematical problem.
